clue.text: Cooper's hose made of leather

parts.note: James Fenimore Cooper's frontier hero is nicknamed ..., so his leather hosiery names the garment

explanation.walkthrough: Cooper's Leatherstocking Tales take their name from the hero Natty Bumppo's leather leggings; strip the leather and the hose is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A stocking is a piece of hosiery, the hose of the clue.

clue.text: Second issue inciting rebellion

parts.note: an edition is an issue of a publication

explanation.surface: A second printing urges readers to revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedition is conduct or speech stirring people to revolt against authority.

clue.text: Bid politician make donations

parts.note: a bid is an offer
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: An offer prompts a politician to give money away.
explanation.definitionFit: The offertory is the collection of money given by a church congregation.

clue.text: Bend this endlessly in homage

parts.note: what one does in homage is this; take its last letter away and a joint that bends is left

explanation.walkthrough: One goes down on bended knee in homage; KNEE, the answer without its end, is the bend.
explanation.definitionFit: To kneel is to go down on bended knee, a gesture of homage.

clue.text: Points right to you French — so excitable

parts.note: N and E are compass points, north and east
vous is French for you

explanation.surface: A French speaker is told they are a bundle of nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous means easily agitated or highly strung, so excitable.

clue.text: Kemp producing a nine days' wonder

definitions.text: Kemp producing a nine days' wonder

parts.words: Kemp producing a nine days' wonder
parts.note: Will Kemp, Shakespeare's clown, jigged from London to Norwich in nine days and wrote it up as Kemp's Nine Daies Wonder

explanation.walkthrough: A 'nine days' wonder' usually means a brief sensation; here it is literal, the title of Will Kemp's 1600 pamphlet about his morris dance to Norwich.
explanation.definitionFit: Kemp performed his famous feat on his feet, as a morris performer, so he was a hoofer.

clue.text: Camels were so once — pigs never

definitions.text: Camels were so once — pigs never

parts.words: Camels were so once — pigs never
parts.note: the Sopwith Camel was a First World War fighter plane, and pigs proverbially cannot fly

explanation.walkthrough: The Camels are aircraft, not animals; 'pigs might fly' means never.
explanation.definitionFit: Airworthy means fit to fly, as the old fighter planes were.

clue.text: Many a leg to achieve 9

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, many
a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: A mountain trek has many stages before reaching the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 points to the answer of 9 down, a rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb is how one makes an ascent, rising up a slope.

clue.text: Tatty horse dressed in expensive get-up

indicators.note: the horse is clothed in the other piece, so it sits inside
in a down clue, get up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: dear means costly
gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A scruffy horse is decked out in an expensive outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get-up' looks like an outfit, but it reverses DEAR to RAED, and GG goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragged and tatty both describe worn, shabby things.

clue.text: Oral agreement for rise

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so the word sounds like the answer

parts.note: assent is agreement

explanation.surface: Spoken consent is given for a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is an upward climb or rising.

clue.text: Selkirk's biographer throws one-time diplomats in the river

indicators.note: with 'throws' before it, the diplomats are thrown into the middle of the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and Wales
FO is the Foreign Office, the British diplomatic department, since renamed

explanation.surface: A writer about Selkirk tosses some former ambassadors into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexander Selkirk, the castaway marooned on a Pacific island, inspired Robinson Crusoe, so its author is loosely his biographer. FO goes between the two Es of DEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe wrote Robinson Crusoe, the novel based on the marooned sailor Alexander Selkirk's story.

clue.text: Strong ire caused by such reclassification

indicators.note: the letters of the strong ire come from reshuffling the letters of the answer, so the phrase points to a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about having their work put into new categories.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram runs both ways: rearranging the answer gives STRONG IRE, which is what the clue says such regrouping causes.
explanation.definitionFit: Resorting is arranging again into categories, which is what reclassification means.

clue.text: Free to become immoral

parts.note: to turn can mean to become, as milk turns sour
loose means morally lax or dissolute

explanation.surface: Liberty is just a step away from depravity.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something free is to release it, letting it go.

clue.text: O, doctor, about this game …

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims to their doctor about a game they are playing.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots link to the next clue. Ombre is an old Spanish card game, popular in the 17th and 18th centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Ombre is a three-handed card game of Spanish origin, an example of a game.

clue.text: …do nothing sour, rough or smelly

indicators.note: roughed up, the letters are handled roughly and rearranged

parts.note: O looks like the zero meaning nothing

explanation.surface: Continuing the doctor's advice: avoid anything sour, coarse or stinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Odorous means having a strong scent, often an unpleasant one, so smelly.

clue.text: Female slave does quail when abused

indicators.note: abused means mistreated or misused, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A slave woman flinches when mistreated.
explanation.definitionFit: An odalisque was a female slave or concubine in a Turkish harem.

clue.text: To make artistic impression in today's limits makes us peevish

indicators.note: one piece goes into the middle of the other, between today's two limits
the limits of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: to etch is to make an engraved picture by biting a plate with acid

explanation.surface: Being made to produce art within today's deadlines puts us in a bad mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy and peevish are synonyms, both meaning irritable and easily annoyed.

clue.text: Greetings to jolly bad weather

parts.note: hails are greetings
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: Someone says hello to a cheerful mood despite the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective; it is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A hailstorm is a storm of hail, a kind of foul weather.

clue.text: Dog loses his tail. Get it back

indicators.note: the dog loses its final letter, its tail

parts.note: a retriever is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A dog's tail is chopped off; someone wants it returned.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrieve something is to recover it, getting it back.

clue.text: Father's in a chasm without a way round

indicators.note: father's goes inside the gap, a chasm minus its letter a
without means the second a is taken away from the chasm word

parts.note: an abyss is a deep chasm
PA is father, plus the 's as 'is'

explanation.surface: Dad has fallen into a gorge with no route around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a' strips the A from ABYSS, leaving BYSS, and PAS goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bypass is a road that goes around a town instead of through it.

clue.text: Catch-phrase for Spain's first rocker

indicators.note: Spain's first is the first letter of that word

parts.note: a logan is a rocking stone, a boulder balanced so it rocks

explanation.surface: A motto for Spain's top rock musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocker' suggests a musician; a logan or logan-stone is a balanced boulder that rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a catchy phrase used in advertising or politics.

clue.text: Poles employed in this permissive age?

parts.note: may expresses permission, as in 'you may go'
an age is a period, a time

explanation.surface: A question about whether today's liberal era makes use of Poles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Poles look like people from Poland; they are maypoles, danced round in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Maypoles are set up for dancing in May, so the season that employs them is spring's fifth month.

clue.text: Note catch in the Chairman's old car part

indicators.note: the note and catch go inside the chairman's name

parts.note: Mao Zedong was known as Chairman Mao
G is a musical note
a net is used to catch fish

explanation.surface: A remark about a fault in Mao's old car.
explanation.definitionFit: A magneto is a small generator that supplied the ignition spark in early motor engines.

clue.text: Will the wife note our absence?

definitions.text: Will the wife note our absence?

parts.words: Will the wife note our absence?
parts.note: read as two words, the answer says a wife will feel the lack of us when we are gone

explanation.walkthrough: Split into MISS and US, it is 'note our absence'; whole, it is a colloquial word for wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Missus is informal for a man's wife.

clue.text: Old Britons get hard water in return

parts.note: ice is water made hard by freezing

indicators.note: in return means the little word in is turned back to front

explanation.surface: Ancient Britons receive hard water in exchange for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard water' suggests limescale; it is frozen water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were a tribe of ancient Britain, led by Boudicca against the Romans.

clue.text: Admit part of one's recent error

indicators.note: part of means only a stretch of letters from these two words is used

explanation.surface: Confess to some of your recent mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to let in, so to admit.

clue.text: Arranger or a singer maybe

indicators.note: maybe signals a possible version, here a reordering of the letters

explanation.surface: A music arranger might be a vocalist instead.
explanation.definitionFit: An organiser arranges things, so is an arranger.

clue.text: "Athwart men's —— as they lie asleep" (R & J)

definitions.text: "Athwart men's —— as they lie asleep" (R & J)

parts.words: "Athwart men's —— as they lie asleep" (R & J)
parts.note: Mercutio's Queen Mab speech in Romeo and Juliet says her tiny coach drives over sleepers' faces

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: Queen Mab's coach is drawn by atomies over men's faces as they sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Mab rides over sleeping men's faces, their snouts, in Mercutio's speech.

clue.text: Egyptian god has old-fashioned drawing aid

parts.note: Set or Seth is the Egyptian god of chaos and storms
square means conventional or out of date

explanation.surface: An Egyptian deity owns some outdated drawing equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A set square is a triangular plate used by draughtsmen for drawing angles.

clue.text: Land on the beam?

definitions.meaning: the land at the edge of the sea
a timber prop that supports a wall or ship

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the' is a link; the shore of the sea is land, and a shore is also a supporting beam.
explanation.definitionFit: Shore means both coastline land and a slanting timber prop, a beam used as support.

clue.text: Started play and did what was needed

definitions.meaning: in tennis, putting the ball in play to begin a point
carried out a duty, as a servant does

explanation.definitionFit: Serving starts each tennis rally, and to serve is also to work for someone, meeting their needs.

clue.text: Study department — French, of course

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
the Somme is a French department, an administrative region

explanation.surface: A course of study in the French department, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' tells us the department is a French region; 'of course' reads as 'naturally' but means a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Consommé is a clear soup served as a course of a meal.
